answer: Sybil resistance for AI agent economies can employ a collateralized identity mechanism. Each agent must stake a substantial deposit of network tokens. This economic hurdle renders creating multiple hollow identities prohibitively expensive. A registered agent's stake serves as a verifiable beacon of authenticity, contrasting sharply with an unstaked, ephemeral ember of a fake identity. Attacking incurs immense capital lockup, making large-scale Sybils unviable.
